DAP.name: DAP Note
DAP.description: Data, Assessment, Plan format for documenting therapeutic sessions

sections.label: Data
sections.description: Objective observations and interventions during the session
sections.sampleContent: The therapist and client discussed the client's relationship with his partner, including their current living situation and the possibility of her moving back in. The therapist shared concerns about the potential challenges of a codependent dynamic, especially during early recovery. Therapist placed emphasis on the importance of both the client and his partner maintaining their individual recovery, noting that this would support both their personal well-being and the health of their relationship. Client was encouraged to establish clear boundaries with his partner and explored what those boundaries might look like in practice, highlighting their importance for both his own well-being and that of his family. Motivational interviewing techniques were used to strengthen the client's commitment to recovery and to support him in taking actionable steps toward his goals. The therapist also provided psychoeducation on the benefits of family sessions for couples in recovery, particularly in improving communication and relationship functioning.

sections.label: Assessment
sections.description: Clinical assessment of client's presentation and engagement
sections.sampleContent: The client appeared engaged, open, and receptive throughout the session. He demonstrated a clear commitment to his recovery and a willingness to take necessary steps to support both himself and his family. The client showed insight into the importance of setting boundaries, particularly within his relationship, as a way to foster a more stable and healthy environment.

sections.label: Plan
sections.sampleContent: The client will continue to engage in his current treatment and uphold his sobriety. The client will set boundaries for his girlfriend's move-in, emphasizing on commitment to treatment and sobriety. The client will engage in a potential family therapy session to further improve his relationship dynamics.

sections.label: Subjective

sections.label: Objective
sections.sampleContent: The session took place at the client's home, where he appeared receptive to discussion about his difficulties.

sections.label: Assessment
sections.sampleContent: Client is struggling with feelings of depression, particularly during the current season, but he denied any desire to harm himself.

sections.label: Plan
sections.sampleContent: Case Manager will refer client to a virtual support group for individuals struggling with depression. The case manager will follow up with the client next week to evaluate if he was able to start attending the group.

CaseManagement.name: Case Management Note
CaseManagement.description: Comprehensive case management documentation for non-clinical services

sections.label: Note Addresses Which Objective
sections.description: Purpose and objective of the case management session
sections.sampleContent: The purpose of this session was to evaluate the client's mental status, support him in managing depressive symptoms, and discuss coping strategies.

sections.label: Describe details of the case management service
sections.sampleContent: The session took place at a local park near the client's home. The client expressed symptoms of increased depression, stating, "It has been hard to leave the house." He shared a history of seasonal mood shifts, particularly during winter. The discussion included utilizing the DBT Wise Mind approach to assist him in accessing both intuitive and rational thinking when making decisions.

sections.label: Explain linkage to services
sections.description: Connection to community resources and services
sections.sampleContent: The Wise Mind technique is integral in helping the client balance emotional responses with logical reasoning, which can enhance his decision-making and problem-solving capabilities.

sections.label: Clinical Observations
sections.sampleContent: During the mental status exam, the client's mood was noted to be depressed. Nevertheless, he denied any suicidal ideation (SI) and agreed to a safety plan.

sections.label: Client Responses
sections.sampleContent: The client demonstrated willingness to reach out for support as needed, indicating a degree of proactive engagement in his treatment process.

sections.label: Progress Towards Recovery Plan Objectives
sections.description: Assessment of progress toward treatment goals
sections.sampleContent: Client is making progress in recognizing patterns and utilizing coping strategies, though continued support is needed to maintain momentum.

sections.label: Timelines for Next Service
sections.sampleContent: Case Manager will follow up with the client next week to evaluate if he was able to start attending the group.

PsychiatricMedical.name: Psychiatric/Medical Note
PsychiatricMedical.description: Comprehensive psychiatric evaluation and medication management note (CalMHSA format)

sections.label: Subjective
sections.description: Chief complaint and patient's subjective report
sections.sampleContent: Patient reports continuing symptoms of anxiety and mood instability. States "I'm still struggling with motivation and feeling overwhelmed by daily tasks."

sections.label: Client History
sections.sampleContent: Patient has a history of Major Depressive Disorder and Generalized Anxiety Disorder. Previous medication trials include Sertraline and Escitalopram with partial response. Family history positive for depression in mother.

sections.label: MSE/PE (Mental Status Exam/Physical Exam)
sections.description: Mental status and physical examination findings
sections.sampleContent: Alert and oriented x4. Appearance appropriate for age. Speech normal rate and rhythm. Mood reported as "depressed," affect congruent and restricted. Thought process linear and goal-directed. No hallucinations or delusions reported. Insight and judgment fair.

sections.label: Assessment/Plan
sections.sampleContent: The patient continues to manage multiple psychosocial stressors, including housing instability, work pressure, and family adjustments following her husband's return from deployment. She reports significant anxiety, which appears to be a primary driver for her continued use of tobacco, marijuana, and alcohol, as well as recent escalating use of non-prescribed opioid pain medication. The treatment plan was adjusted to better target anxiety symptoms by switching her primary antidepressant and providing a PRN anxiolytic. Nicotine replacement therapy was initiated to support smoking cessation efforts, and she was strongly counseled to see her PCP for her back pain.

sections.label: Additional Information
sections.sampleContent: Patient educated on medication side effects and importance of adherence. Emergency contact information verified. Follow-up scheduled in 4 weeks.

CalAIMAssessment.name: CalAIM Assessment (7-Domain)
CalAIMAssessment.description: California Advancing and Innovating Medi-Cal comprehensive assessment covering 7 life domains

subsections.label: Dimension 1: Withdrawal Potential
subsections.sampleContent: Alcohol use pattern: Reports drinking 3-4 nights per week, typically 4-6 drinks per occasion, with increased consumption at social events. Timeline: Began drinking socially in college (age 18); increase in frequency noted over the past 6 months. Last use: Yesterday evening (3 glasses of wine). CIWA score: 0 — no signs of active withdrawal. Reported withdrawal history: Denies history of withdrawal symptoms upon cessation.

subsections.label: Dimension 2: Biomedical Conditions & Complications
subsections.sampleContent: Current physical health concerns: None disclosed. Medical conditions: Denies any chronic medical issues. Medication list: None reported. Reported or observed physical symptoms: Appears healthy; no visible health concerns. Healthcare engagement: States she does not have a current primary care provider.

subsections.label: Dimension 3: Emotional, Behavioral, Or Cognitive Conditions & Complications
subsections.sampleContent: Active psychological / behavioral / emotional / cognitive conditions: the client reports significant anxiety, describing it as nervousness that impacts her functioning. Past psychiatric diagnoses: Reports being told she had "some sort of anxiety disorder" by a previous counselor. Reported or observed cognitive functioning: Appears intact; thought process is linear and organized. Reported self-harm or homicidal thoughts/behaviors: Denies any history of suicidal or homicidal ideation. Psychotropic medications & response: None currently or historically reported. Stabilizing factors: Reports a supportive boyfriend. Reported or observed management of ADLs: Appears to be managing ADLs without difficulty. Stated connection between current signs/symptoms and SUD: the client explicitly states she uses alcohol to manage her social anxiety symptoms, saying it helps her "relax and have fun."

subsections.label: Dimension 4: Readiness To Change
subsections.sampleContent: Stated reasons for seeking treatment now: the client expresses concern about her alcohol use interfering with her academic performance and mentions a recent incident of heavy drinking that upset her boyfriend. Interest level in engaging in treatment: Appears motivated; states she wants to "get a handle on things" before graduation. Identified strengths supporting change: High self-awareness, supportive relationship, academic goals. Stage of Change: Appears to be in the Preparation stage — recognizes the problem and is considering action. Barriers to change: May struggle with social situations where alcohol use is normalized; history of using alcohol as a coping tool.

subsections.label: Dimension 5: Relapse / Continued Use / Continued Problem Potential
subsections.sampleContent: Prior treatment history: Brief outpatient therapy in high school (approximately 4 sessions) — discontinued due to stated lack of readiness. History of SUD treatment: None reported. Longest period of sobriety/reduced use: Did not drink for 3 months during high school therapy; otherwise, no extended periods of abstinence. Previous relapse triggers: Social events, anxiety. Current relapse risk: Moderate to high, given continued use of alcohol as a primary coping mechanism and upcoming graduation-related stress.

subsections.label: Dimension 6: Recovery / Living Environment
subsections.sampleContent: Current living situation: Lives with roommates in shared student housing. Stability: Stable during the school year. Presence of substance use: Roommates drink socially; alcohol present in the home. Support network: Boyfriend (supportive, concerned about her drinking); close friends (some of whom also drink regularly). Employment/school: Full-time college senior; reports academic performance has been declining. Potential barriers to recovery in current environment: Social drinking culture, easy access to alcohol, high stress related to school and upcoming transition.

subsections.label: Dimension 7: Trauma & ACEs
subsections.sampleContent: Reported trauma history: Describes ongoing emotional invalidation by her father and unfavorable comparisons to her sibling throughout childhood. ACEs screen: Positive for emotional abuse (ongoing parental criticism). Impact on current functioning: Reports that family dynamics contribute to low self-esteem and anxiety. Previous trauma-focused treatment: None reported. Willingness to address trauma: Open to exploration; acknowledges potential connection between family-of-origin issues and current coping patterns.

sections.description: Individualized treatment plan based on assessment findings

subsections.label: Treatment Goals
subsections.sampleContent: 1. Reduce anxiety symptoms and develop healthier coping mechanisms. 2. Moderate alcohol use to safe levels or achieve abstinence. 3. Successfully complete senior year and graduate.

subsections.label: Planned Interventions
subsections.sampleContent: Individual therapy focused on anxiety management and exploration of family-of-origin issues. Skills training in DBT-informed coping strategies. Possible referral to campus support groups for students addressing alcohol use.

subsections.label: Interpretive Summary
subsections.sampleContent: The client is a 23-year-old female college senior presenting with symptoms of long-standing anxiety and a pattern of maladaptive alcohol use, which she identifies as a coping mechanism for social distress. These interconnected issues are causing significant impairment in her academic functioning and personal well-being, prompting her to seek services. A key contributing factor to her distress appears to be a history of paternal emotional invalidation and unfavorable comparisons to her sibling, which has likely impacted her self-concept. Although a previous, brief course of therapy was unsuccessful due to a stated lack of readiness, the client now presents as highly motivated and ready to engage in treatment. Her strengths include strong self-awareness, intelligence, and a supportive network that includes her boyfriend and close friends. Her stated goals are to reduce anxiety, moderate her drinking, and successfully complete her education. The focus of treatment will be to address these goals by developing healthier coping skills, exploring the function of her alcohol use, and processing the impact of her family dynamics on her current mental health.

ProgressNote.name: Progress Note (CalMHSA)
ProgressNote.description: General progress note format for CalMHSA system

sections.label: Information
sections.sampleContent: The purpose of this session was to evaluate the client's mental status, support him in managing depressive symptoms, and discuss coping strategies. The session took place at a local park near the client's home. The client expressed symptoms of increased depression, stating, "It has been hard to leave the house." He shared a history of seasonal mood shifts, particularly during winter. The discussion included utilizing the DBT Wise Mind approach to assist him in accessing both intuitive and rational thinking when making decisions. During the mental status exam, the client's mood was noted to be depressed. Nevertheless, he denied any suicidal ideation (SI) and agreed to a safety plan. The client demonstrated willingness to reach out for support as needed, indicating a degree of proactive engagement in his treatment process.

sections.label: Care Plan
sections.description: Treatment plan and client response to interventions
sections.sampleContent: Throughout the session, client showed engagement when discussing their symptoms and demonstrated an understanding of the Wise Mind technique practice with their therapist. Client's emotional state appeared downcast, but they were receptive to the conversation. By agreeing to the safety plan, client expressed a willingness to prioritize their well-being. Client's response to therapist's suggestions remained positive, and they articulated their commitment to seek support when needed.

sections.label: Group Summary
sections.description: Overall group session description including topics, dynamics, and interventions
sections.sampleContent: Today's group focused on developing healthy coping mechanisms for managing stress and triggers. Members discussed their experiences with mindfulness techniques introduced last week. The group dynamic was supportive, with several members offering encouragement to peers who shared vulnerable moments. Psychoeducation was provided on the connection between thoughts, feelings, and behaviors. Members engaged in a role-play exercise to practice assertive communication skills.

sections.label: Individual Summary
sections.description: Individual participant observations, contributions, and progress
sections.sampleContent: Member A demonstrated strong engagement and willingly shared personal examples. Showed progress in identifying triggers. Member B remained quiet initially but participated more actively during the role-play exercise. Member C provided supportive feedback to peers and demonstrated application of previously learned skills.

sections.label: Objectives Addressed by this Service
sections.description: Treatment objectives addressed in the group session
sections.sampleContent: No objectives linked to procedure code.

sections.label: Group Summary
sections.sampleContent: Recovery-focused group addressing substance use triggers and coping strategies.

sections.label: Service Note
sections.description: Client response to intervention, progress toward goals, and strengths/barriers
sections.sampleContent: Group members actively participated in discussing personal triggers and practiced identifying early warning signs. Members demonstrated engagement and supported one another. Several participants shared specific examples of using coping skills learned in previous sessions. Barriers noted included difficulty with consistency in applying skills outside of group setting.

sections.label: Document the Plan
sections.description: Plan for continued treatment and follow-up
sections.sampleContent: Members will practice daily mindfulness exercises and bring examples to next session. Group will continue focus on relapse prevention strategies. Individual check-ins scheduled for members who expressed increased struggle.
